workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> FIXME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [PROVED]
watchme: none, because its proof bin/proofs/test_cairn_resolves_from_powershell.py is the whole of its correctness; the live check is the same command on akiendell; the code lives at bin/cairn.cmd

fixme.missing: off Windows each tooth must print '  FAIL <tooth>: ... UNRAN ...' so a non-Windows reseal writes no red (64ae0df3f1f3)

answer.text: Off Windows both teeth raise UNRAN through one guard (_windows_only), and a failing tooth prints '  FAIL <tooth>: <Type>: <msg>', the line shape the tester's not-run rule reads (cairn/devices/tester/device.py unran_only, ticket 64ae0df3f1f3). A Linux reseal then writes no seal and leaves the standing one untouched, so bin's component_color stops redding from a host that cannot run the proof. Measured 2026-11-22: the Linux reseal at 0be5c74ca sealed it red (plain RED line; tooth 2 had no host guard, FileNotFoundError cmd.exe); after the change unran_only reads both teeth as not-run on this box. The green seal still comes only from a native Windows run.
